title: National Gallery of British Art opens
documented_change: The Millbank gallery opens under the National Gallery's wider governance and becomes known as Tate.
why_it_matters: British art gains a dedicated home, but Tate is not yet the independent statutory body it later becomes.
what_remained: The collection remains embedded in National Gallery governance.

title: Separate Tate trustee structure
documented_change: Post-war legislation establishes a separate Tate Board while retaining a formal National Gallery link.
why_it_matters: Institutional autonomy increases while an explicit governance bridge survives.
what_remained: The national collections remain legally connected through board representation.

title: Museums and Galleries Act
documented_change: The Act establishes the modern Tate and National Gallery corporate Boards and functions.
why_it_matters: Creates the current statutory basis and preserves reciprocal trustee appointment.
what_remained: Arm's-length trusteeship and the cross-board relationship remain.

title: Tate Modern opens
documented_change: A major new London site opens for international modern and contemporary art.
why_it_matters: Changes Tate's scale, reach and organisational complexity without rewriting core statutory governance.
what_remained: National-collection responsibilities remain with Tate's Board.

title: DCMS framework 2025–28
documented_change: The framework specifies current ministerial, Board, appointment and spending relationships.
why_it_matters: Makes PM appointments, Board chair selection, Director approval and National Gallery cross-appointment explicit.
what_remained: The framework operates alongside the 1992 Act.
